bib.title: SpecAugment: A Simple Data Augmentation Method for Automatic Speech Recognition

question: Can a simple augmentation applied directly to log mel spectrograms make end-to-end ASR networks beat hybrid systems on LibriSpeech and Switchboard?
hypothesis: Features robust to time deformation, partial frequency loss and partial loss of short speech segments help the network learn useful features and reduce overfitting.
contributions: SpecAugment: time warping, frequency masking and time masking on the log mel spectrogram, applied online
State-of-the-art WER on LibriSpeech 960h and Switchboard 300h with LAS, with and without an LM
Observation that augmentation turns overfitting into underfitting, so bigger networks and longer schedules help

method.summary: Three deformations (time warp, frequency mask, time mask) are applied online to the log mel spectrogram as if it were an image. LAS encoder-decoder networks are trained with long ramp-hold-decay learning rate schedules, then optionally decoded with shallow fusion of an RNN LM.

datasets.name: LibriSpeech 960h
datasets.split: dev-other for checkpoint selection; test-clean/test-other for reporting
datasets.preprocessing: 80-dim filter banks with delta and delta-delta; 16k word piece model built from training transcripts; log mel normalized to zero mean

datasets.name: Switchboard 300h (LDC97S62)
datasets.split: no canonical dev set; checkpoint at end of schedule; test Hub5'00 SWBD and CallHome
datasets.preprocessing: 80-dim filter banks with delta and delta-delta; 1k WPM from Switchboard+Fisher transcripts

models.name: LAS-d-w (LAS-4-1024, LAS-6-1024, LAS-6-1280)
models.architecture: Listen Attend and Spell: 2-layer CNN with max-pooling and stride 2, then d stacked bidirectional LSTMs of cell size w, 2-layer RNN decoder of cell dimension w

other.LAS-4-1024: the large model of Irie et al. 2019

training.lr_schedule: ramp up from zero to sr, hold, exponential decay from si to sf down to 1/100 of max, constant after. (sr,snoise,si,sf): B=(0.5k,10k,20k,80k), D=(1k,20k,40k,160k), L=(1k,20k,140k,320k)
training.warmup: ramp-up over sr steps (0.5k B, 1k D and L)
training.steps: B ends 80k (Switchboard evaluated at 100k); D 160k; L 320k (Switchboard reported at 340k)
training.regularisation: variational weight noise std 0.075 turned on at snoise; uniform label smoothing 0.1; SpecAugment
training.compute: 7 days for the Table 2 runs; ~24 days for schedule L

other.label_smoothing_policy: LibriSpeech: off in Table 2 runs; with L on only for steps < 140k; Switchboard: on throughout with L, both tried with B
other.policies: Table 1: None W0; LB W80 F27 mF1 T100 p1.0 mT1; LD W80 F27 mF2 T100 p1.0 mT2; SM W40 F15 mF2 T70 p0.2 mT2; SS W40 F27 mF2 T70 p0.2 mT2
other.other_hyperparameters: all other hyperparameters fixed, no additional tuning

inference.samples: single run per configuration; no seeds stated

parameters.shallow_fusion: y* = argmax_y (log P(y|x) + lambda log P_LM(y)) plus coverage penalty c
parameters.switchboard: (lambda,c) = (0.3,0.05), (0.2,0.0125), (0.1,0.025) for the three entries of Table 5, grid search on RT-03

baselines: HMM, CTC/ASG and LAS systems in Tables 3 and 5
eval.protocol: LibriSpeech: checkpoint chosen by dev-other, test reported. Switchboard: end-of-schedule checkpoint. No significance tests or repeated runs.

evidence.quote: on 32 Google Cloud TPU chips for 7 days

limits: Single runs, no seeds or confidence intervals; differences of 0.1 WER (time warp ablation) are within plausible noise
Policies are hand-crafted; no search over policies
Checkpoint for Switchboard chosen at schedule end because there is no dev set
Fusion parameters for Switchboard do not transfer between networks and need per-model grid search
Label smoothing destabilizes training under augmentation with decaying LR
Very long compute: about 24 days on 32 TPU chips for the best models
Only LAS evaluated, English read and conversational speech, no noise or far-field test
Optimizer, parameter counts and code not stated
